name: Black-Box Design System

source.status: project copy reconstructed from the approved contract supplied in the project brief

artDirection: Late-1990s PlayStation survival-horror. Recovered flight-safety hardware and black-box instrumentation frame the island, rather than a modern web dashboard.

typography.display: Silkscreen for short labels and headings only
typography.body: IBM Plex Mono for readable body copy, values, forms, and timers
typography.avoid: Pixel fonts for long body copy

tokens.borders: Square, thin metallic borders with hard shadows and worn-metal texture; no rounded SaaS surfaces.

gameplay.columns: left roster 32%, central gameplay 47%, right utilities 21% (adapt to content and min widths)
rules: Show incident report when result phase is active, not necessarily simultaneously with voting.
Aftermath is an end-state; do not permanently reserve layout for it during normal play.
Visual reference depicts multiple states together for demonstration; runtime UI follows game phase.
The UI ELEMENTS / TOKENS panel is design-documentation only, not a player-facing feature.

responsive.medium: gameplay 2-zone with utilities moved below; lobby survivor grid adapts
responsive.small: single-column reading order; panels stack; survivor cards 1 or 2 columns by available width; decision choices stack when needed
responsive.overflow: avoid clipping long names, settings, modal/timer and critical actions

keyboard.escape: back/close if existing functionality provides it
keyboard.arrowKeys: optional roving navigation for survivor grid; do not override form fields

accessibility: Focus visible on all actionable controls
Maintain contrast and readable body text
Render timers and status changes with appropriate accessible updates

backgrounds.sharedEnvironment: Same crash site and color grade as original lobby
layering: optional global CRT overlay with pointer-events none

portraits.preferred: Existing approved low-poly character models or renders
portraits.consistentFraming: Same camera angle and crop across roster/selection

textures.preferred: Small tileable scratched-metal/noise maps or CSS layered gradients
textures.avoid: Heavy full-resolution unique images for every panel

nonnegotiables: One shared PanelFrame, SurvivorCard, CharacterPortrait, StatusBadge and ActionButton library across lobby and game.
Never revert gameplay settings to a purple solid rectangle.
Never revert incident reports to flat salmon/pink dashboard cards.
Never use bright beige as default for manifest, survivor cards, resources or choices. Beige is reserved for aged incident paper.
Keep same flight identity, boarding code, and story-specific language.
Do not alter networking, game mechanics, resource math, timers, host permissions, or persistence.
No hardcoded demo player names, status values, vote totals, resource values, or session codes.
Use game phase to control which components appear; composite mockups are not a single required runtime layout.
doNotUse: large cream surfaces on normal panels
body text with aggressive CRT distortion
acceptanceChecklist: Lobby and gameplay visually look like the same game.
Every gameplay panel except paper report uses dark worn metal plus nearly-black inset.
Paper report has aged parchment interior in metal framing.
Settings has dark metal backing, never a purple rectangle.
Character selection looks identical across screens and uses actual game art.
Network warnings and status badges use shared design tokens.
Voting is legible at 1080p and preserves live state/timing.
Background art never contains baked-in UI.
No gameplay metrics or demo states are hardcoded.
All controls usable with keyboard and readable with reduced effects.
